I will keep it close to what has worked here before. I have 10.9 mu total, and I will split it like this: 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, and 2.9 mu in cotton. I do not like taking big risks with new things. I will use the kind of seed and fertilizer rates I have seen work on nearby fields with well water, and I will lean a little heavy on fertilizer rather than come up short. Wheat is my main steady crop, so I will feed it well and give it 3 irrigations if the season is normal. After wheat harvest, I will put maize on the same 8 mu right away, using hybrid seed because that is what gives grain around here. Cotton takes more watching, especially for insects, so even on the smaller area I will spray it more times. I do not count things like a technician. I look at what brought grain last year, what neighbors are doing, and what I can afford for 10.9 mu without squeezing the whole family too hard. I will spend money first on seed, fertilizer, and water, because if yield falls, that loss is bigger than the cost of a few extra bags.
